column8: At 13 weeks in Northern Ireland, hoping for a midwife-led unit; asks for resources.
column9: I’m also looking for recommendations for hypnobirthing books, courses, podcasts, or apps. Any general recommendations for pregnancy, birth, and the postpartum period would also be really appreciated.

column8: Thanking commenters for midwife-led unit and hypnobirthing tips.
column9: I know birth can be out of your control a lot of the times so this is me planning for my best case scenario

column8: Her loose plan for labour after a previous caesarean.
column9: Not sure if I’ll be able to cope with hypnobirthing alone but planning on using gas and air.

column8: At 35 weeks with her fourth, ten years after her last; what people remind her.
column9: I’m expecting my 4th baby, my first little girl. In a sense starting all over as people like to remind me.

column8: At a routine appointment she felt pushed towards a repeat caesarean.
column9: At my routine appt w my ob/gyn today I felt like I was being pressured to just accept having a c-section.

column8: Wanting a say this time, unlike with her first babies.
column9: As this is my last child I want to feel heard and understood. I was so young w my first two especially & really didn’t realize that I had a say in anything.

column8: Her OB wrote a letter starting her leave early; she works on her feet.
column9: he did write a letter to start my leave from work early (I’m entitled to approx 14 weeks total). I work on my feet all day long so I somewhat appreciate the early leave to rest & prepare for baby girl.

column8: Told to "enjoy it" while describing waking to pee four times a night.
column9: I was talking about how I have to get up to go pee like 4 times a night and she responded “enjoy it”.

column8: She wants a child but not the process of pregnancy.
column9: I really want to have a child but I don’t enjoy the process of being pregnant. I’m just excited for the end result. I don’t like feeling ill most of the day.

column8: At 18 weeks: it was her mother-in-law who said "enjoy it".
column9: It was my mother in law that made the “Enjoy it” comment. She was also really perturbed by what I ordered at a restaurant that night. She didn’t think it was enough.

column8: On remarks about her bump.
column9: But yeah stupid comments from people galore. I don’t like it when people comment about my size, either me being big or small, both make me self conscious.

column8: Barista at 9 weeks with her second; coffee now makes her gag and her toddler stays up late.
column9: My toddler refuses to sleep till late, and pregnancy is making me EXHAUSTED and whenever I work morning I don't get more than 5 hours of sleep and it's KILLING me not to have caffeine

column8: Symptoms differ from her first pregnancy.
column9: this is my second pregnancy I'm 9w1d and with my first I didn't have any symptoms, but this one has been a wild ride so far.. I'm a big coffee drinker and enjoyer, but I just can't stand coffee anymore, even smell of it makes me gag (ironic because I work as barista).

column8: Hoping the second trimester brings relief.
column9: I'm hoping my symptoms are gonna get easier once I hit second trimester and I'll be able to drink my morning coffee again.

column8: The caffeine limit her OB gave her.
column9: my OB told me everything under 250 is ok.

column8: First pregnancy at 37, symptoms easing at 7-8 weeks, booking appointment still over a week away.
column9: Everyday I say to myself any symptoms are symptoms which keeps me calm most of the time but not having my midwife appointment yet and being able to ask them I just would love some responses.

column8: Her boyfriend's relentless optimism when she worries.
column9: Not being able to talk so openly about it all doesn't help. My BF is great but hes a golden labrador and everything is good and happy, so when I have doubts he doesnt fully understand it.

column8: Considering a private early scan while waiting for NHS care.
column9: Haven't had my first midwife appointment yet, due to my holiday its on the 10th of june, hoping scan wont be long after that and if we are worried I may go for a private scan

column8: At 38 weeks, a friend with a newborn keeps asking for details and offering items.
column9: Around 3-4 months ago she started to ping me more often, like every few days and asked about some details like fetus weight. I started to feel a bit overwhelmed by the frequency of it.

column8: Her answer to the friend's offers.
column9: I told her that we already have everything and don't want to gather too many items in advance, but that I am thankful for consideration.

column8: What she wants once her son is born.
column9: I don't want to be in this "mom club" vibe with her and prefer to go back to the old, light dynamics we used to have […] I don't want this kinda talk to continue after my son is born, I want to avoid comparing the milestones, weight etc.

column8: At 40+2, still active and working out, blaming everyone's easy-birth predictions.
column9: I’m still active and working out, I’m afraid everyone in my life that kept saying my baby is just going to pop out and I’ll have an easy labor jinxed me.

column8: At 18 weeks living in a renovation with a toddler; the decorator won't give an end date.
column9: The decorator won’t commit to when he’ll be finished and the house is covered in dust and we also have a toddler.

column8: First-time mother at 29 weeks starting to dread visits after the birth.
column9: I'm currently 29 weeks pregnant (FTM) and the dreaded "first visits" after he's born are starting to pop into my mind.

column8: Her view of older relatives.
column9: older generations of grandparents and aunties who think the baby is property of everyone and who think they know everything and that brand new parents don't know anything.

column8: Part of the visitor list she has drafted.
column9: No visits at the hospital, and no visits at home for the first few weeks so we can bond as a family of three.

column8: Torn between a rules list and losing family closeness.
column9: I really don't want to isolate us whatsoever, or create a "terms-of-service agreement" to visit the baby.

column8: Visitor rule lists seem to her an online trend.
column9: I’ve noticed a trend here and on TikTok where parents create a massive list of rules that they send out to family and friends before the baby is born. In my personal experience, I’ve never had anyone send me this type of list (I think they are a bit uncommon in my country)

column8: Unsure what the newborn days will feel like and whether she will want visitors.
column9: I'm also a FTM and I have absolutely no clue on what it feels like to have a newborn "in real life". Will I feel amazingly? Will I bleed pp for weeks? Are people going to stomp over our boundaries or in reality they are going to be super chill? Will I miss having people around after a couple of days?

column8: Her mother's daily messages after the announcement.
column9: when I told my parents I was pregnant, my mother kept sending me text messages every single day asking if baby was alright. Like, every single day. If I didn't respond immediately, she would call my partner at work.

column8: Why she wants rules set before the birth.
column9: I end up feeling like I'm crossing a line and being rude and I end up feeling extremely guilty about it. I don't want to deal with that in my postpartum period.
